insights: **What drives predictions most.** Initial estimate (42% of total attribution), Initial estimate / weekly wage (12% of total attribution), Injury nature (10% of total attribution) are the three strongest drivers. Together the top five account for 77%.

**The claim description matters.** Features derived from the free text (Injury nature, Body part, Injury cause, Description length) carry 22% of all attribution: a smaller but real part of what the model knows comes from the description alone.

**The adjuster's estimate is informative but not taken at face value.** Moving from the lowest tenth of initial estimates (<= 1,000) to the highest (>= 40,510) changes the model output by x13.84 on average, while the estimates themselves differ 40.5-fold: the model shrinks extreme estimates towards what similar claims usually cost.
**Reporting delay has little systematic effect** in the model (x1.00 from fastest to slowest tenth).
**Injury type shifts costs strongly.** Relative to the average claim, the injury nature alone moves predictions by x1.75 for soft tissue claims and x0.75 for foreign body claims.

**Age matters, but less than the type of injury.** The oldest tenth of claimants (>= 53) gets x1.13 the attribution of the youngest (<= 20): older workers' claims cost more, consistent with longer recovery.
